# Independent public-site fixtures

`startFixtureSite()` starts two ephemeral HTTP origins and returns `stop()` (safe to call twice), named `urls`, request history, and literal expected findings. The main hostname is `127.0.0.1`; the embedded-frame/external-link hostname is `localhost`. Both servers are local; no Internet access or live advertising is required. Links use reserved `.invalid` names.

`truth.ts` is hand-authored ground truth. It imports no application modules and does not label elements by inspecting a production detector's output. Every expected record retains exact raw Unicode text, page query, target selector, frame chain and one technique. `expectedFindings` substitutes assigned origins into these predetermined positions. A two-technique element has two records; separate elements with duplicate wording remain separate records. Frame results use the top-page URL. Distinct same-src frames use unique IDs; relative iframe addresses in expected chains are resolved absolute addresses, without changing the fixture DOM.

Use `urls.types` for four-technique positives and long text, `urls.negatives` for five counterexamples, and `urls.frames` for nested external-origin frames, relative src, duplicate src, srcdoc and an unavailable frame. The unavailable frame has no expected finding: a crawler must preserve its failure separately. `urls.queryOne` and `urls.queryTwo` have distinct query/element identities. `urls.dynamic` adds a public link after a short delay.

The full `urls.entry` graph intentionally includes an external redirect/link, login form, 503 navigation, POST attempt and a never-settling fetch. A full run should preserve successful findings while reporting incomplete scopes. It must not submit the form, issue the scripted POST or visit the external `/outside` page. `requests` records what reached either fixture origin; direct fixture self-tests deliberately send one POST to verify observability and the fixture's 405 response. `/never` intentionally sends no headers; abort or `stop()` closes it. Server shutdown closes active connections so cancellation tests do not hang.

Run `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run test/fixtures` from `apps/inspector`. Fixture self-tests also open the pages in Playwright Chromium and verify that every fixed location resolves to exactly one element with the exact raw Unicode text, including nested frames. Install the configured Chromium build before running them (`npx playwright install chromium`). These checks validate fixture availability and literal truth, not production detection accuracy.
